editorial:
Imagine being a tired single mom who hasn't slept in years, trying to raise a wild kid while dealing with a huge loss in your life. That is where you start with this story. You get to know Amelia and her son, Samuel, who live in a gray, lonely house that feels like it is closing in on them. Things get weird when a creepy pop-up book about a monster called the Babadook appears out of nowhere. Once you read the book, the monster starts showing up in the house. The vibe is super tense, and you can really feel how stressed out the characters are as they start to lose their grip on reality.

What really makes this work is the acting. The lead actress does an amazing job showing how grief can make a person snap. The scares are a bit slow, but they hit hard when they finally happen. If you like movies that mess with your head rather than just using loud noises, you will love this. It is a great pick for a rainy night. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, but if you want the best picture, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for those dark, moody scenes.
endingExplained: You find out the monster is not a ghost, but a symbol of the mother's sadness and anger. In the end, she does not kill the monster because she cannot just erase her grief. Instead, she beats it and forces it into the basement. She learns to live with her pain and be a better mom. The movie wraps up with her keeping the monster locked away while she finally finds peace with her son.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves horror movies that have a deep emotional meaning.
